term_monthly_units.assumption: Scout gives no direct top-10-20-ASIN unit-volume figure, only a qualitative '1K+ bought in past month' badge on the primary term's top listing (search_terms notes) as the highest apparent-volume signal. Base case extrapolates that one leading ASIN's ~1,000+ units/month across an estimated 5-8 comparably-ranked page-one/two ASINs on 'elbow rest pad for desk' and its close synonyms (forearm rest pad, desk edge elbow cushion), giving ~6,000/month; ±40% per the brief's instruction gives 3,600-8,400.

share_m6.assumption: Brief's framework: a new entrant reaches 1-5% of term volume in months 1-3 and 3-10% by months 6-12 if CTR/conversion beat the median. Buyer's own purchase_probability_current (click 0.55, add_to_cart 0.4, buy 0.5) already exceeds a generic median because the visible stepped cross-section and spec badge answer fear #1 in the thumbnail and gallery — but competition's copycat_risk base case puts the first clone at month 2, so by month 6 the clone wave is already live in the grid. This share_m6 base of 3.5% sits at the low-to-mid end of the 3-10% band specifically because it already assumes some early erosion from clones undercutting at $8-13, not the clean pre-clone window.

share_m12.assumption: Share continues to soften from m6 to m12 as more quantity-first clones enter (competition's price_war shows win_probability dropping from 0.55 before clones to 0.30 after, and choice_rank falling to 3rd), so this range already bakes in ongoing organic erosion on top of the m6 numbers — it is not the pre-clone case. The engine's own separate clone-wave Monte-Carlo (run from price_war.share_haircut_pct = 30%) applies a further, formal haircut on top of this already-eroded base; the two are not meant to be added, the engine handles that re-run.

monthly_units_m12.assumption: term_monthly_units × share_m12 at each percentile; lower than m6 because share_m12 already reflects further clone-wave erosion per the note above, even before the engine's own cloned-volume Monte-Carlo re-run.

annual_units_y1.assumption: Ramp-weighted sum of 12 months, not a flat multiply. Months 1-3 (moore.chasm, innovator-only, pre-review-base) average ~40% of the month-6 run rate; months 4-6 ramp linearly to the m6 level; months 7-9 hold near the m6-m12 midpoint; months 10-12 get a Q4/holiday seasonality lift ('organise my life'/gift-adjacent office gear) that roughly offsets the ongoing clone-driven share erosion. Base case: 3×(0.4×210) + 3×150 + 3×195 + 3×190 ≈ 1,857, rounded to 1,850; low/high scaled proportionally from the monthly_units_m6/m12 low/high bands.

forecast.seasonality_note: Back-to-school (August) and back-to-office/New Year 'organise my life' (January) per scout's trends note on the seasonal computer-desk-elbow-pad term; Q4 (Nov-Dec) gets a general gift/office-refresh lift but is also when Amazon's storage_alloc_usd rises per the brief's peak-season note, compressing month-11/12 contribution even as units tick up.
forecast.reasoning: Outside-in: scout's only volume signal is a '1K+ bought in past month' badge on the category leader, not a summed top-10-20 figure, so term_monthly_units is a wider, explicitly-labelled extrapolation rather than a scout-sourced number, widened the required ±40%. Attainable share starts inside the brief's 1-5% band for months 1-3 (innovator-only, per moore.chasm) and is placed at the low-to-mid end of the 3-10% months-6-12 band specifically because competition's copycat_risk (base 2 months to first clone) means the clone wave is already live well before month 6 — these share numbers are the already-eroding, not the clean pre-clone, case. The engine's separate clone-wave Monte-Carlo re-run (from price_war.share_haircut_pct=30%) is an additional, formal reduction layered on top by the engine itself, not something genius adds by hand here.

premortem.obituary: It is 12 months on and a factory-direct clone undercut us at $9-11 within 10 weeks of launch, copying the visible two-tone stepped silhouette closely enough that shoppers scanning thumbnails couldn't tell the density difference, and our choice-rank slid to third on the page.
premortem.mitigation: Matches competition.copycat_risk (level 'high', months_to_first_clone base 2, high 4) almost exactly — not contradicted here. Mitigation is the two moats innovaty and competition both name: file the stepped-taper design registration before launch (blocks exact-mold copies) and keep the printed, load-tested density badge (a spec a quantity-first factory has no incentive to verify), plus watch competition's watch_signals (new sellers adopting the silhouette, page-one price drops below $13-14) to reprice or push ads faster.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Design-registration filing fee plus the FTO/legal-lever cost already budgeted in tooling_and_nre; incremental cost here is the registration filing itself, not the full FTO search.

premortem.obituary: It is 12 months on and the flame-bonded foam layers or the rubber-base bond delaminated at the edges after 6-9 months of daily shear load, exactly the failure mode the buyer's own durability_instinct flags from a past mousepad base, and 1-star reviews started citing 'peeling' and 'lopsided.'
premortem.mitigation: I1/I3 already specify flame-bonding across the full contact face and mechanical keying instead of perimeter gluing, per innovaty's durability_review. Mitigation is enforcing the ASTM D3574 Test D and 90-degree peel/shear test gates (already budgeted as the test rig line) as a hard QC pass/fail before every production run, not just at prototype stage.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Incremental per-batch retest cost on top of the one-time test rig already in tooling_and_nre, assuming quarterly batch verification in year one.

premortem.obituary: It is 12 months on and the packaged dimensions came in 2mm over the small-standard size-tier line, bumping the FBA fee up a full tier and quietly erasing the contribution margin the plan was priced on.
premortem.mitigation: Lock packaged dimensions with a 3-5mm safety margin before the steel production tool is cut, and verify with Amazon's own FBA size-tier calculator before the first production run ships, not after.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Essentially a design-review step; cost is the engineering time to re-check dimensions against the tier line, not new tooling.

premortem.obituary: It is 12 months on and the China tariff moved again — F8's ~33.9% effective rate climbed further — and duty alone ate the contribution margin that was modeled at the base case.
premortem.mitigation: Qualify a second co-packer in Vietnam in parallel with the China tooling so volume can shift without a full re-tool if tariffs spike again; keep the price band's high end ($22.99) as headroom to absorb a duty increase without going unrealistic on the buyer's max_with_reason ceiling.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Cost of qualifying and sampling a second-country supplier as a hedge, not a full second tooling run.

premortem.obituary: It is 12 months on and Amazon flagged the '20% recycled SBR content' claim on the rubber base for insufficient substantiation and suppressed the listing detail page pending review, stalling sales for two weeks during the ramp.
premortem.mitigation: Keep only the supplier-certificate-backed recycled-content claim (already scoped in innovaty's sustainability.claims, with the certificate referenced by the packaging QR code) and avoid any broader 'eco-friendly' or 'sustainable' language the certificate doesn't cover; be ready to pull the claim from copy without any product change if flagged.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Copy-edit and compliance-review time only; the underlying certificate is already a supplier deliverable, not a new cost.

premortem.obituary: It is 12 months on and review velocity never crossed the chasm — months 1-3 stayed innovator-only volume, the review count sat under 50 while VAYDEER's 2,045-review lead kept winning the social-proof scan, and the listing never reached page one.
premortem.mitigation: The foam-swatch press-test insert (innovaty's bundle_or_addition) plus the first ad budget line are both designed to shorten this exact window — the swatch answers fear #1 at unboxing before first use, and the launch ad spend buys the review velocity a 40-80% ACoS is meant to purchase; add an automated post-purchase review-request flow at negligible incremental cost.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Cost of a review-request automation tool/service on top of the ad budget already in tooling_and_nre.

premortem.obituary: It is 12 months on and factory QC drift on the base-layer foam density (say 38kg/m3 shipped instead of the specified 45kg/m3+) meant real units still let the desk edge press through for heavier forearms, so complaint cluster C1 came right back under our own brand and the spec badge became a liability, not an asset, once reviewers called it out.
premortem.mitigation: Incoming-lot density testing (ISO 845) on every production batch before FBA check-in, not just at T1/prototype sign-off, with a hard reject threshold tied to the same 45kg/m3+ spec printed on the badge; ties the badge's honesty to a repeatable QC gate rather than a one-time prototype test.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Per-year incremental cost of batch-sample lab density testing on top of the one-time compression-set rig already budgeted.

idea_rulings.why: The hero mechanism keeps landed cost well inside the sanity zone (base $3.47 landed against a $19.99 price is ~17% of price, under the brief's 30% red-flag line) while directly answering the category's #1 complaint (C1, 35% of negative sentiment) with a thumbnail-visible shape.
idea_rulings.deciding_number: landed cost is ~17% of price at base case (well under the 30% landed/price rail)

idea_rulings.why: A printed insert and embossed base icon cost pennies and directly close three of the buyer's five ranked fears (fit, orientation) with no tooling risk.

A full-bond rubber base is a dimes-tier upgrade over a thin strip that removes the exact delamination failure mode the buyer names from personal experience, and it doubles as a competition-named moat.

Costs more than innovaty's 'cents' tag suggests once priced as a real DWR-finished double-knit (own estimate, $0.42/unit base), but still stays cheap enough not to threaten the sanity rails, and it removes complaint cluster C2 entirely rather than mitigating it.
idea_rulings.deciding_number: $0.42/unit incremental cost (higher than innovaty's cost_tier label, still realistic)

idea_rulings.why: A woven spec tag is the cheapest idea in the set and is the specific mechanism that converts a copyable claim into a moat a quantity-first cloner has no incentive to verify, per competition's spec_edge moat.

It is a free mold-geometry change with no incremental unit cost, but it only serves need N5, the lowest-severity unmet need in buyer.json, and innovaty itself defers it to v2 pending real Q&A/return-reason signal — correctly sequenced as a stretch add, not a v1 requirement.
idea_rulings.deciding_number: need N5 severity = 3/10, the lowest of the five needs targeted

regulatory: No CPSC, electrical or child-safety review triggers for a passive foam/fabric/rubber desk accessory with no magnets or hardware (I6's magnet-adjacent concerns from the knowledge base do not apply — this product carries no magnet).
Prop 65 labelling review needed for the foam/rubber/dye chemistry typical of Chinese-manufactured foam products sold in California.

Recycled-content (SBR) and OEKO-TEX-adjacent claims must be backed by a retained supplier certificate before printing on packaging, per innovaty's own sustainability.claims scoping, to survive a critic/Amazon substantiation check.
three_sentences_to_founder: Landed cost runs $1.96-$5.82 per unit (base $3.47, about 17% of the $19.99 base price) against a $17.99-$22.99 price sitting inside the buyer's own $24 max-with-a-visible-reason ceiling, so the economics have real room before the engine's sanity rails start flashing.

Fixed launch cost is $38k-$120k (base ~$67k), driven mostly by two separate foam and rubber steel tools plus the FTO search that I1's medium prior-art risk makes mandatory — that is the number that makes this a stretch, not a slam dunk, feasibility call.

Competition already rates this arena high copycat-risk (first clone in 1-4 months, a 30% forecast-volume haircut once it lands), so I1's design registration, I5's spec badge and I2's fit diagram are the plan's actual moat, not nice-to-haves — ship v1_now with all five ideas together or the plan loses its reason to exist above $18.
